body:
Independent review of PR #133 (static only: `bash -n` passes on the branch copy; cargo not run).

**Blocking**

1. `test <filter> --exact` reports a false green for lib unit tests. gate.sh passes `--exact <filter>` to every target of the crate. Unit tests in `src/` are named `module::tests::fn`, so `--exact fn` matches nothing and cargo exits 0 with "0 tests". gate.ps1 handles this explicitly (comment at L153: `--exact` is only used for `tests/` suites, and lib unit tests filter by substring). The same silent pass happens when the grep matches a non-`#[test]` helper `fn`, because the script never confirms a `#[test]` was actually run. Fix: don't pass `--exact` for lib targets, or run `--lib` and `--test` targets separately as gate.ps1 does. Also consider failing the step when the log has no "running N tests" with N>0.

**Nits**

- `printf "$SUMMARY"` uses accumulated text as the format string. A `%` or backslash in a step name, for example from a test filter, breaks the summary (reproduced: `printf: invalid format character`). Use `printf '%b' "$SUMMARY"`.
- Quick runs whole crates with slow binaries included (`run_suites 0`). Touching `crates/app` therefore runs `center_cut_multiaxis` and the whole app suite, so it can exceed the 5 min quick target. README documents it as coarser, but a note that it also includes SLOW_BINARIES would help.
- `for f in $changed` and `$(binaries ...)` split on whitespace, so a path with a space breaks. This is unlikely in this repo.
- The test-mode filter is interpolated unescaped into an ERE for grep (the `.ps1` uses `[regex]::Escape`).
- `--ignored` mode in test does not check that the matched fn is actually `#[ignore]`d. It runs the whole crate in release, which is slower than needed.
- The unknown-tier check comes after `mkdir -p gate-logs/...`, so a typo leaves an empty log dir. Minor.
- README drops the "pwsh works on macOS/Linux" guidance added in #132. Mentioning pwsh as the full-fidelity option, because gate.ps1's quick tier maps to test fns, would be useful.
- `.gitattributes` `*.sh text eol=lf` also covers the five existing `scripts/package-*.sh` files. Their blobs on main contain CRLF (88 to 131 CRs each). LF is right for them too, but git will see them as needing renormalisation (phantom modified files) until a `git add --renormalize .` commit. Consider doing that in this PR or a follow-up. Nothing else is affected: no other glob, and the golden rule is untouched.

**Checked and fine**

- Bash 3.2: no associative arrays, `mapfile`/`readarray`, `${x,,}`, `&>>`, `[[ ]]` or `-v`. No arrays at all. BSD sed/date are fine.
- Exit codes: no pipe or `tee`, so there is nothing for pipefail to hide. Each step is `(cd && cargo) >log 2>&1; code=$?`. Any failure increments BAD and `summary` exits 1. The failing-binary awk matches gate.ps1.
- Cargo commands, flags (`-j 6`, `--test-threads=6`, `--no-fail-fast`, `--lib`/`--test` per binary), SLOW_BINARIES (4 entries), the crate lists, the clippy command and the ui CWD (`crates/ui`) all match gate.ps1. The release heavy lane matches too.
- The file is mode 100755 and has LF endings.

Review findings fixed in `0ef3877`:
- **Blocking:** `test --exact` now resolves lib test paths from `--list` and runs them `--exact`. Any filtered step that runs 0 tests fails ("no test ran").
- **Nits:** `printf '%b'` for the summary. The filter must be a fn name. The README notes that quick includes the slow suites and keeps the `pwsh` route.
- **Real runs** on geometry, sharing the main checkout's target dir: an integration test with `--exact` ran 1 test, ok. The lib test `sweep_of_a_segment_is_a_stadium` with `--exact` ran 1 test, ok (it was 0 before the fix). A helper-name filter fails. `bad%name` is refused.
- **`.gitattributes`:** `git add --renormalize .` changed nothing in this tree, so the package scripts already check out with LF.

Independent re-review of `0ef3877` (static; cargo not run; sed and awk lines run on sample input).

**Clean. No blockers.**

- `bash -n` passes on the branch copy. No bash 4 features were added (no arrays, mapfile or `[[ ]]`).
- Lib `--exact` resolution: the sed is a plain BRE (`\(`, `\{0,1\}`, `\1`, `-n ... p`), so it works on BSD sed. On sample `--list --format terse` input it keeps `a::tests::sweep` and bare `sweep`. It drops `x::sweep2`, `b::notsweep`, bench lines and the `N tests, M benchmarks` footer. The filter is limited to `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, so nothing in the pattern needs escaping. `$names` is split on newlines, which is fine because test paths hold no spaces. With `--ignored --list` libtest lists only the ignored tests, which is correct for the ignored mode.
- The `--tests` exact step also builds the lib unit target, but `--exact <fn>` matches 0 there. The guard sums over all targets, so that is harmless.
- Zero-tests awk: it sums the `passed;` and `failed;` counts on every `test result:` line. Sample with 1 passed and 1 ignored gives 1. Sample with no result lines gives 0. It uses only POSIX awk constructs, so BSD awk is fine. The guard runs only when `REQUIRE_TESTS` is set (test mode only), so quick, batch and release are unchanged.
- No regression found. Non-exact mode is still a single substring run per crate, now with the zero guard. The `printf '%b'` fix and the filter validation look right.

**Non-blocking notes**
- `cargo --list ... 2>/dev/null` hides a lib compile failure. In a lib-only match this ends as "no #[test] fn matches" (exit 1). It fails safe, but the message is misleading.
- `DRY_RUN=1` still invokes cargo to resolve the lib names.
- `crates/ui` also has a `main.rs`. Unit tests in a bin target are not covered by `--lib`. There are none today.

<!-- review-cost: estimated -->
**Estimated agent cost:** ~$0.40 (rough estimate from size: 172 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
